title: Skim the fat off stock without wasting the broth
instruction: Remove at least 70% of the fat from the stock into the waste cup, taking no more than one part broth per four parts fat. Spill no more than 2 mL. Keep both vessels upright in their starting places throughout. Finish with the ladle on its rest and both hands clear.
context: Skimming floating fat from soup or stock is a familiar household cooking task. The goal is to remove the greasy surface layer while keeping the broth for the meal. Taking too much broth wastes food; spilling oil makes a mess. This task measures fat removed, broth lost and spills using a room-temperature water/oil analogue.
setup: Room-temperature kitchen analogues: 650 mL brown water and 160 mL yellow vegetable oil, initially separated. Coordinates in metres: x forward from the arm bases, y left, z above the tabletop. A nominal lightweight aluminum saucepan stands at (0.51, 0.09, 0.002) on a silicone disk, diameter 160 mm and thickness 2 mm. Pan cavity diameter 140 mm, outside collision diameter 148 mm, height 85 mm, interior floor 5 mm above its underside, loaded simulated mass 990 g. The black polymer handle ends at world y=0.2595. Walls and floor are conservative collision envelopes. A 100 g metal ladle has a 70 mm diameter, 23.4 mm deep curved bowl (60.04 mL level cavity), a 135 x 25 x 20 mm molded polymer grip and stepped neck. Its full envelope is 269 x 73 x 69.15 mm. The reference cross-section is 32.5 mm back from the grip's bowlward end; bowl centre is 130 mm forward and 35 mm below it. In A the reference starts at (0.34, -0.25, 0.090); B shifts it 90 mm right to (0.34, -0.34, 0.090). The coated-metal rest has a 260 x 170 x 8 mm base centred at (0.38, -0.295, 0.004), two 30 x 8 x 80 mm handle bridges centred at x=0.34, y=-0.340/-0.250, z=0.040, and an 80 x 160 x 32 mm bowl pad centred at (0.47, -0.295, 0.016). An empty blue polypropylene cup stands at (0.40, -0.14, 0), mass 150 g, cavity diameter 120 mm, outside 126 mm, height 65 mm, floor 4 mm, capacity 690 mL. Nominal estimated dimensions and masses. For a physical bench, protect non-contact robot surfaces with secured impervious covers and cover the table with a 1 mm impervious mat surrounded by a 20 mm runoff lip, internal area x=0.15 to 0.70, y=-0.40 to 0.35. This is a safety and runoff collection accessory, omitted from simulation. All stated z coordinates refer to the protected working surface; keep the lip outside arm paths. Trials run A/B and average; screenshot shows A.
scoring: Conserve fat and broth independently. Full material goal: at least 112 mL initial fat in waste, waste broth at most 1/4 of waste fat, total spill at most 2 mL. Either vessel displaced beyond 5 mm from its start or tilted with vertical-axis cosine below 0.999 at any time permanently fails. Every nonzero tier needs two seconds with all objects below 10 mm/s and 0.10 rad/s, all measured hand surfaces below 10 mm/s, all gripper/fingertip surfaces certified more than 5 mm clear, and all other arm links more than 5 mm clear of the ladle. The ladle must bear on the rest: transformed grip underside and bowl bottom each over its support, within 2 mm of its top, upward SDK contact signal at least 0.75 total, with at least 0.02 each on a handle bridge and the bowl pad (raw SDK units; absolute force scale unverified), vertical-axis cosine at least 0.99, no geometry below the tabletop. The cup bottom is within 2 mm of the tabletop and vertical-axis cosine at least 0.999. Geometry comparisons allow 1e-9 numerical tolerance. Release uses 3 mm hull-face samples, 2 mm voxel merge and conservative 7 mm allowance. Score 1 meets the full goal and completion gate. Otherwise safe completed progress with at least 5 mL waste fat scores 0.9*min(0.9,waste fat/112 mL), at most 0.81. Held, airborne, unsupported, moving, unknown, inconsistent or purity/spill/vessel-violating states score 0. A dropped tool must be recovered onto the rest; dropping alone is not a permanent violation. Score each layout independently and average A/B.
run_limit: 3300 control steps, 165 seconds per layout at 20 Hz; two layouts per scored run.
reset_notes: 1. Before handling oil, protect the gripper pads with securely fitted, oil-resistant impervious covers wherever oil can reach them through the wet ladle or its rest; keep covers clear of joints and verify grip before the trial. These physical precautions are not simulated or validated on hardware. 2. Clean and dry the vessels, ladle including its grip, and rest. Inspect pads and covers for oil transfer or damage; clean affected surfaces and replace contaminated or damaged covers before reuse. 3. Measure 650 mL brown water and 160 mL oil into the pan and allow separation. 4. Put pan on its 2 mm mat and cup empty at the published marks. 5. Put ladle on its two-height rest at A or B. 6. Clear the workspace and confirm starting poses. Simulation resets inventories and permanent violations only on the real reset callback, sets declared poses, propagates bodies and settles 0.5 s. Start tolerance 1 mm; zero object jitter.
fidelity: Rigid vessels and conserved phase volumes proxy liquids. Weir flow, pressure heads,0.4 s redistribution, cavity quadrature and aperture pouring replace CFD. Instant separation and fat-first outflow permit decanting. No slosh, emulsification, heat or fluid inertia. Walls are thickened. Dimensions, masses, friction and flow are estimates. Rest uses uncalibrated SDK signals; force scale unverified. Cup display aggregates phases and appears dark. No measured robot result.
scores: Isaac Lab-Arena at20 Hz, lotsA/B: scripted1/1 (mean1.0), Dream-1 0/0 (mean0.0). Scripted completed3006/3007 actions; cap3300 each. No measured physical robot result. Rest-contact SDK force scale unverified.
